findings.explanation: Root discovery through .gitmodules reaches locally nested data and software, but the raw-input child points its source module at a host filesystem location. Partial is defensible for recursive source completeness in the declared scope; this does not establish a missing input to the top-level statistical rerun.

Following root > data/raw_eyegaze reveals src/lab-eyetracking with a machine-local acquisition URL. That is a concrete portability/reachability defect, while the other root links are public repository references. The assessment correctly avoids claiming that any online retrieval failed.

The root Docker recipe includes analysis/rendering software, but root > labels > compute_all.sh resolves python from the host and merely adds code/remodnav to PYTHONPATH. Its linked setup.py lists libraries without enclosing the execution environment, so partial is supported.

Frozen file inventory identifies Git blobs for the code, text, configuration and documentation, plus pinned child repositories. Omitted payloads in the review package do not negate version control. Overriding a tree-clean packaging failure is appropriate.

The inventory records annex symlinks and MD5E content keys for image blobs and large inputs; the linked data README explicitly describes separate content storage using git-annex. This supports the versioning property without asserting available payload bytes.

The inspected root run has exit 0, image extra_inputs and explicit result outputs. In contrast, the label-producing record only invokes a shell script whose interpreter and libraries are supplied by the host. Exact-environment provenance therefore covers only part of the declared object.

The root updated instructions are coherent and accurately distinguish the old route. However, the explicitly included label component tells readers to run Condor preprocess/detect scripts, while its production record invokes compute_all.sh. The assessment recognizes this undisclosed conflict elsewhere but omits it here. Native verdict rule 10 caps A.1 instruction items at partial when documentation and production mechanisms disagree.
findings.suggested_correction: Change met to partial for the stated recursive scope; retain credit for the root README and cite the linked README versus the recorded label command.

findings.explanation: There is a clear top-level rerun command, but the documented entry into the included label-production component is stale relative to the recorded bash command. Native rule 10 explicitly applies mechanism-versus-record and documentation-versus-mechanism mismatches to must/008. Root-only evidence cannot justify met across the assessment's broader scope.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial, distinguishing the supported top-level entry point from the conflicting linked entry point.

findings.explanation: The root loaders construct repository-relative input paths. The discoverable linked scheduler generator literally emits a user-specific initial directory and a fixed interpreter path. Because the linked README still directs users toward this legacy procedure, these are relevant defects rather than incidental archived text.

The recipe declares scientific and manuscript tooling, and the root README identifies external orchestration prerequisites. The included label script still obtains python and its libraries from the ambient host. That concrete component gap supports partial without treating every unpinned Debian package as an undeclared dependency.

Partial remains supported by the non-root Docker permission assumption and linked scheduler configuration. The rationale overstates the mount-documentation gap: .datalad/config explicitly says that PWD is mounted at /tmp and explains temporary HOME. The adapter is discoverable through root README version guidance and the registration.
findings.suggested_correction: Keep partial, but credit the documented mount/HOME behavior and focus the gap on Docker permissions and the linked host-specific scheduler assumptions.

findings.explanation: The root requirements are listed, but the linked README describes a different algorithm/Condor procedure and does not supply a requirements list for the recorded REMoDNaV shell route. The positive root evidence and concrete linked gap justify partial.

Environment descriptions and the image registration are committed beside code; dependency declarations also exist in the linked package. This criterion asks whether specifications are version-controlled, so incomplete dependency freezing belongs in other items and does not negate this evidence.

History contains executable image build/save commands and a later recorded conversion of an existing image in response to Docker compatibility changes. Thus this is more than a single introduced file or an aspirational update statement. The duplicate flag correctly identifies the repeated should/008 question.

The archived root image has an exact config/layer identity, and latest is only a saved label; that correction of the probe is sound. Nevertheless, the included label-production environment has neither an image nor a frozen dependency manifest. A pinned REMoDNaV source revision plus unversioned numpy/scipy/statsmodels/matplotlib requirements cannot support exact environment replication across this object.
findings.suggested_correction: Change met to partial while retaining the archived-image strength and the probe override. Explicitly name label generation as the uncovered environment.

findings.explanation: The published frozen source includes the environment recipe and saved-image manifest; the inspected annex log records a public URL for the referenced layer. This supports sharing of the specification, with payload availability today remaining untested. It is correctly distinguished from proof of a successful download.

The root tells readers how to install orchestration tools, clone and run the saved image. The linked label README does not explain how to obtain the environment for the current recorded script. Partial is consistent with the actual documentation coverage.

Root and nested components use Git revisions, and large data uses the associated git-annex mechanism. The frozen graph confirms a common tracking system even though some content is unavailable to this review.

The historical analysis run is actual execution evidence, but the later conversion only tests container launch with exit 0. Root inventory has no recurring study workflow test, and linked Travis tests the package. Partial appropriately credits episodic verification without treating package CI as regular manuscript reproduction.

Raw input, label derivatives and software are independently linked, and the root keeps analysis code, image files and figure outputs in distinct locations. Separation is visible structurally and is not invalidated by uninstalled modules in an inspection clone.

Public access is explicitly asserted for the published dataset, but a machine-local source module does not by itself establish that it is restricted or public. Keeping this classification unresolved is justified; neither an all-public N/A claim nor an inferred restriction is established by the available terms.

The recorded analysis command actually invoked the archived-image adapter and reported exit 0; the inspected adapter constructs docker run --rm. Together these constitute historical evidence of a pipeline test in a fresh container, which the native method permits instead of a new reviewer rerun. This does not establish that every upstream label computation was isolated.

The root launches a new removable container, whereas the recorded label shell loop directly reuses host python and inherited PYTHONPATH. Partial accurately distinguishes these execution models and avoids claiming that persistent mounted outputs prevent container ephemerality.

The saved root environment has actual historical use and a later recorded launch/conversion check. Neither record establishes regular reconstitution checks, and the frozen root inventory contains no scheduled/CI testing mechanism. Partial is reasonable for demonstrated episodic checks with no regularity evidence.

The tracked object represents an archived image with exact blob references and annex keys, rather than only naming a registry image. The cohort's deliberate omission of those blobs does not show that the object failed to archive them.

The same build/save procedure and later Docker-compatibility conversion inspected for must/014 support this duplicate item. Matching verdicts and upstream-duplicate flags are appropriate; the two answers should remain synchronized.

Following explicit Gitlinks discovers both dataset inputs and nested software/test-data dependencies. The criterion asks whether external components are linked as modules, so a problematic source URL under must/002 does not erase the presence of modular links.

Root documentation gives the major roles and a reproducible composition route. In the linked label component, the documented Condor stages fail to explain the actual pinned REMoDNaV/compute_all composition. Partial reflects a concrete documentation gap, not a demand for a particular diagram format.

Updating the linked REMoDNaV revision after label production proves a version change, not a boundary that breaks independent updates. Gitlinks keep the parent composition fixed, and the later root run consumed the pinned published labels. The assessment explicitly concedes no observed broken run, so its absence-of-rerun argument does not demonstrate the specific violation required for partial.
findings.suggested_correction: Assess the interface/boundary design directly. Credit independent Gitlink pinning; if compatibility cannot be settled without execution or interface evidence, use not-checked for that unresolved property rather than calling missing rerun provenance a demonstrated modularity defect.

findings.explanation: Gitlinks determine module versions, the container registration dispatches the workflow, and Makefiles connect statistical outputs, figures and manuscript rendering. Those are concrete composition mechanisms even though some linked reproduction documentation needs repair.

The root README and module metadata support navigation. The linked label README omits the current compute_all entry and software-module relationship, limiting understanding of the recursive structure. Partial is supported by inspected documentation.

limitations: Inspection only: no scientific execution, image build, payload retrieval or network request. Missing payloads are cohort omissions, not observed retrieval failures. Historical exit codes are recorded evidence, not newly verified results.

Used only the assigned anonymized JSON, frozen manifest/source/history and assigned native instrument. Raw assessor probe products and its narrative report were outside the assigned review input, so their detailed outputs and presentation were not independently audited.

Verified the frozen manifest SHA256 and native checklist lock; native response validation passed for all 31 answers. The input contains 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY responses, with one not-checked SHOULD retained; no aggregate numerical score is supplied to audit. Validator success was not used as substantive support.

The external adapter citation in the assessment uses release tag 1.2.3 rather than a commit hash. This review identifies the frozen adapter with its manifest SHA256; no live tag resolution or actual runtime-version verification was performed.
The unresolved raw-source module and present-day public payload availability remain unverified. Agreement records evidentiary support, not human approval.
